name: Matrix
description: All-in-one Matrix homeserver for Unraid: Synapse + coturn + Element Web (/element/) + Ketesa admin UI (/admin/). Plug-and-play — just fill in SERVER_NAME and Postgres connection, everything else is generated automatically. OPTIONAL, OFF BY DEFAULT: delegated authentication via Matrix Authentication Service, which is what makes QR code device linking ("Link new device" in Element) possible. Leave the Delegated Auth field alone and the container behaves exactly as before. Enabling it needs a second empty Postgres database and a second reverse-proxy host with HTTPS, and it changes how your users sign in — read the README section "Delegated Auth and QR Code Login" first. PREREQUISITES (before starting the container): 1) PostgreSQL database — connect to your Postgres container and run: CREATE USER matrix WITH PASSWORD 'yourpass'; CREATE DATABASE matrix ENCODING 'UTF8' LC_COLLATE='C' LC_CTYPE='C' TEMPLATE template0 OWNER matrix; (UTF8 + LC_COLLATE='C' is mandatory — Synapse will refuse to start otherwise.) 2) Reverse proxy (Nginx Proxy Manager) for matrix.yourdomain.tld → Unraid-IP:8008. In the proxy host → Advanced tab, add: client_max_body_size 100m; proxy_read_timeout 600s; (Without these, media uploads fail and long-running requests time out.) 3) Federation discovery works out of the box: Synapse serves /.well-known/matrix/server and /.well-known/matrix/client itself on the API port (8008), so the proxy host from step 2 already covers them. No extra Custom Locations needed (remove any manual ones from older setups). Full step-by-step guide (NPM screenshots, well-known, first user): https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/matrix#readme

paths.name: Data Directory
paths.description: Persistent data: homeserver.yaml, media, signing keys. Never delete — destroys keys and breaks federation.

paths.name: TURN-TLS Certs
paths.description: Optional. Mount a folder containing fullchain.pem + privkey.pem to enable TURN-TLS on 5349.

ports.name: Matrix HTTP API
ports.description: Synapse HTTP API. Expose via reverse proxy with HTTPS — never directly to the internet.

ports.name: Element Web + Synapse-Admin
ports.description: Serves Element Web (/element/), Synapse-Admin (/admin/) and /.well-known/matrix/* endpoints.

ports.name: TURN TCP
ports.description: TURN/STUN over TCP for voice/video calls. Open this port in your router/firewall.

ports.name: TURN UDP
ports.description: TURN/STUN over UDP for voice/video calls. Open this port in your router/firewall.

ports.name: TURN TLS TCP
ports.description: TURN over TLS (TCP). Optional — only if TLS certs are mounted.

ports.name: TURN TLS UDP
ports.description: TURN over TLS (UDP). Optional — only if TLS certs are mounted.

ports.name: TURN relay ports (UDP)
ports.description: UDP relay port range for TURN (voice/video calls). Must match the container's coturn min-port/max-port.

ports.name: Prometheus Metrics
ports.description: Prometheus metrics at /_synapse/metrics. Bind to a private network only.

ports.name: Auth Service (MAS)
ports.description: Matrix Authentication Service. Only listens when Delegated Auth is set to true. Needs its own reverse-proxy host (e.g. auth.yourdomain.tld) with a certificate.

variables.name: Matrix Server Domain
variables.description: Your Matrix domain, e.g. matrix.yourdomain.tld. Used in Matrix IDs (@user:matrix.yourdomain.tld). Cannot be changed later without wiping the DB.

variables.name: Anonymous Usage Reporting
variables.description: Send anonymous usage stats to Matrix.org. 'yes' or 'no'. Recommended: no.

variables.name: Enable Federation
variables.description: true = chat with the public Matrix network. The container now serves /.well-known/matrix/* itself (serve_server_wellknown) as long as https://SERVER_NAME/ is routed to Synapse — no extra proxy rule needed. false = private island.

variables.name: Enable Registration
variables.description: false = accounts created by the admin only (recommended). true = open self-service signup WITHOUT verification (shows Element's Create Account button) — only enable behind a CAPTCHA or on a trusted network, or you will get spam signups.

variables.name: Delegated Auth (QR login)
variables.description: false = normal Synapse logins (default, unchanged). true = start Matrix Authentication Service and delegate authentication to it, which is what makes QR code device linking possible. Switching this on is a one-way trip for existing accounts: they stay in Synapse until you run 'mas-cli syn2mas migrate', and after that only a database restore gets you back. Read the README section 'Delegated auth' first. It also needs its own reverse-proxy host and breaks encrypted bridges.

variables.name: Auth Public URL
variables.description: Required when Delegated Auth is true. Public https URL of the auth service, e.g. https://auth.yourdomain.tld/ — point a second reverse-proxy host at this container's port 8090. Must be https: the auth service rejects plain-http redirect URLs and Element's sign-in then fails.

variables.name: Auth Database Name
variables.description: Required when Delegated Auth is true. Name of a SEPARATE, EMPTY PostgreSQL database for the auth service — it cannot share Synapse's. Create it with: CREATE DATABASE mas TEMPLATE template0 ENCODING 'UTF8' LC_COLLATE 'C' LC_CTYPE 'C';

variables.name: Auth DB Host
variables.description: Optional. Leave empty to reuse the PostgreSQL host above.

variables.name: Auth DB User
variables.description: Optional. Leave empty to reuse the PostgreSQL user above.

variables.name: Auth DB Password
variables.description: Optional. Leave empty to reuse the PostgreSQL password above.

variables.name: Auth: allow registration
variables.description: Only relevant when Delegated Auth is true. Self-service signup through the auth service's own web UI. Registration through Synapse is impossible under delegated auth, so this replaces Enable Registration.

variables.name: Auth: migrate accounts (ONE WAY)
variables.description: Only relevant when Delegated Auth is true, and only needed once. true = migrate your existing Synapse accounts into the auth service on the next start, before Synapse comes up. BACK UP YOUR DATABASE FIRST: this cannot be undone once anyone has signed in afterwards. Users keep their sessions and are not signed out. It refuses to run if the pre-flight check fails, and it never runs twice. You can leave it on true afterwards, it is a no-op once done.

variables.name: Auth: QR code login
variables.description: Only relevant when Delegated Auth is true. Enables MSC4108 so Element offers 'Link new device' with a QR code. Leave on unless you have a reason not to.

variables.name: TURN Domain
variables.description: Optional. Public hostname clients reach TURN (voice/video) at. Leave empty to use SERVER_NAME; set a dedicated subdomain (e.g. turn.yourdomain.tld) to route TURN around a reverse proxy.

variables.name: TURN Port
variables.description: Optional. Public TURN port advertised to clients (default 3478). Change only if you remapped the published TURN port.

variables.name: PostgreSQL Host
variables.description: IP of your PostgreSQL server (e.g. Unraid host IP). 192.168.1.10 is a placeholder — replace it with your server's IP. IP+port is more reliable than container names.

variables.name: PostgreSQL Port
variables.description: PostgreSQL port. Default 5432.

variables.name: PostgreSQL Username
variables.description: Postgres user for Synapse. Must already exist (see README — Postgres setup).

variables.name: PostgreSQL Password
variables.description: Password for the Postgres user above.

variables.name: PostgreSQL Database
variables.description: Synapse database name. Must be created with ENCODING UTF8, LC_COLLATE='C', LC_CTYPE='C' — see Overview.

variables.name: Matrix Admin Username (Element / Synapse-Admin login)
variables.description: Optional. Localpart of the admin user to auto-create on first boot (e.g. 'admin' → @admin:SERVER_NAME). Logs into Element Web + Synapse-Admin. Clear after creation.

variables.name: Matrix Admin Password (Element / Synapse-Admin login)
variables.description: Optional. Password for the admin user above. Clear after first boot.

variables.name: Timezone
variables.description: Container timezone (affects log timestamps).

variables.name: User ID (PUID)
variables.description: UID Synapse runs as. Default 99 (nobody on Unraid).

variables.name: Group ID (PGID)
variables.description: GID Synapse runs as. Default 100 (users on Unraid).
